facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported-fact base is adequate to underwrite a first view, and it is cleaner than the carve-out history suggests because the standalone capital structure has been in place since November 1, 2025. On filed figures, net sales were 4,300 for nine months 2026 against 3,564 a year earlier, and Adjusted Operating EBITDA was 1,345 against 1,091. Total debt of 4,019 at September 30, 2026 compares with 1,124 of cash and a fully undrawn 1,250 revolver (1,238 after letters of credit). Calculated leverage is 2.37x total and 1.71x net on LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA, down from 2.79x and 2.16x at FY2025. Three points temper this. First, the EBITDA measure excludes indirect legacy costs (84 in nine months 2026) and transformation, integration and other charges (123), which are real cash outflows. Second, interest cover on LTM interest expense flatters the run rate, because the LTM window includes a quarter in which the term loan was outstanding for only two months. Third, FY2025 and nine months 2025 are carve-out periods, so year-on-year changes in interest, tax and allocated costs mix a basis change with performance. The covenant headroom cannot be read from the sources: the maintenance test and its level are disclosed, the issuer's reported ratio and its covenant EBITDA definition are not.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: Adjusted Operating EBITDA is defined as pre-tax earnings before interest, depreciation, amortization, non-operating pension and OPEB items, foreign exchange gains and losses, indirect legacy costs and significant items (Q3 p:39). It is not covenant EBITDA, and it is not a GAAP measure. It adds back items that were cash costs in nine months 2026: indirect legacy costs (84 in the income statement; 114 of cash in the release free-cash-flow bridge, R3 p:11), transformation, integration and other charges (123 in the income statement; 84 of cash, R3 p:11) and a foreign tax cost of the separation (52, R3 p:11). The release prints Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 607 for nine months 2026 against calculated operating cash flow less capex of 357; the difference is these three items (see Calculations). The company's total debt (4,019) is carrying value, net of unamortized discount and issuance costs; the face value of notes and term loan is about 4,100 at December 31, 2025 (K p:120). Net sales and EBITDA comparatives in the releases for Q3 2025 are pro forma (R3 p:2) and are not used.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Qnity Electronics, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated supplier of consumable materials to semiconductor fabrication and to electronics interconnect, reported in two segments, Semiconductor Technologies and Interconnect Solutions. It became independent on November 1, 2025 through a pro-rata distribution by DuPont de Nemours, Inc., and its shares have traded on the New York Stock Exchange since November 3, 2025. The credit-relevant structure is a stand-alone, widely held company with no sponsor, whose debt was raised just before the distribution, at the issuer level with subsidiary guarantees, and was paid out to the former parent. The debt amount was set in connection with the separation. Operating strength is evident in the filings: volume-led sales growth in both segments, driven by AI-linked demand in advanced nodes, advanced packaging and thermal management, and a consumable revenue model. Two features constrain the creditor view. First, customer contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments and the top ten customers are concentrated, so revenue visibility rests on customer forecasts that can be cancelled. Second, Qnity has contractually taken on a share of DuPont's legacy liabilities and some tax exposure under agreements negotiated before it had an independent board. Post-separation behaviour is documented as a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase programme, a borrower-favourable term loan repricing and debt amortization. No document shows priming, uptiering, drop-downs or collateral release. Missing is any executed document or management presentation, so terms and management's own capital allocation priorities are visible only through filing summaries.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt was raised in two steps before the distribution. On August 15, 2025 the issuer sold senior secured notes due 2032 and senior unsecured notes due 2033, each guaranteed by every subsidiary that is a borrower or guarantor under the credit facilities, with the secured notes sharing first-priority liens pari passu with the credit facilities (K p:116 to p:118). On October 31, 2025 it entered a credit agreement for a seven-year term loan and a five-year revolving facility, and the annual report states that the full term loan, together with the notes proceeds, was paid directly to DuPont as a cash dividend in connection with the separation (K p:119). The aggregate principal incurred in connection with the spin-off is stated as 4.1 billion (K p:43), and the financial base handoff carries the instrument-level terms, the maturities and the liquidity position. The use of proceeds is therefore a documented distribution to the former parent, recorded in the cash flow statement as net transfers to the parent. This is a debt-funded distribution at separation, made when the parent still controlled the subsidiary and set its terms; the annual report states Qnity had no independent board or management team representing its interests while the separation agreements were negotiated (K p:45).

This is a debt-funded distribution at separation, made when the parent still controlled the subsidiary and set its terms; the annual report states Qnity had no independent board or management team representing its interests while the separation agreements were negotiated (K p:45).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Since the distribution the documented actions are a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase authorization, a repricing of the term loan and scheduled amortization. The repricing, effective July 1, 2026, cut the margin on term SOFR borrowings from 2.00% to 1.75% with no material change to principal, maturity, amortization or covenant structure, and carries a 1.00% premium on repricing events for six months (Q3 p:20); it is a borrower-favourable amendment to a creditor-owned instrument, not a creditor-adverse one. The amendment document itself is not supplied. Liquidity effect: the financial base shows an undrawn revolver and cash, with no facility expiring within twelve months. Status of every transaction item is final and closed; the only open items are contingent legacy payments to DuPont described under governance below.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Qnity Electronics, Inc. has a moderate-leverage, well-funded credit profile with earnings quality that is weaker than the headline ratios suggest. The strongest support is financial: total debt of USD 4,019 million is 2.37x LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA, liquidity is USD 2,362 million, the revolver is undrawn to October 2030 and no large maturity falls before 2032. The weakest point is the durability of the cash behind those ratios. Demand is volume-driven, cancellable and concentrated in a few customers, adjusted EBITDA leaves out legacy and transformation cash costs, and a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities sits outside debt. The outcome will be decided by whether AI-linked volume growth persists while cash after interest, legacy payments and shareholder returns keeps reducing leverage. Covenant headroom cannot be verified from the sources.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage fell and liquidity is ample. Qnity Electronics, Inc. reports total debt of USD 4,019 million against cash of USD 1,124 million and a fully undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver (USD 1,238 million after letters of credit), so liquidity is USD 2,362 million [CP-1]. Total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x, down from 2.79x at FY2025, and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x against 2.16x. Debt maturities are USD 24 million a year to 2030 and USD 3,980 million after that, so the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033, beyond the revolver's October 2030 expiry. The mechanism is that EBITDA grew while debt was little changed; the implication is low near-term refinancing risk and a cushion against an earnings shortfall.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, the adjusted measures overstate cash available for creditors. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow less capex was USD 357 million, against company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million; the USD 250 million difference is transformation cash costs, indirect legacy payments to DuPont and a separation foreign tax cost [CP-1]. Qnity also paid USD 125 million in dividends and buybacks in the same period. Debt reduction therefore depends on cash that is smaller than adjusted figures show and is shared with shareholders, with the restricted payment baskets not known.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Qnity Electronics, Inc. has moderate and falling leverage: total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x [CP-1; Documentary Fact from a CP-1 figure]. It has deep liquidity of USD 2,362 million, with no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 785 million of its USD 1,124 million cash held in foreign subsidiaries, which may limit how much is freely available in the United States [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its debt is long-dated, with scheduled amortisation of about USD 24 million a year and the notes and term loan due in 2032 and 2033 [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its operating base is growing on volume in both segments, with an LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA margin of 30.9% on USD 5,490 million of LTM net sales [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact, with the margin a company measure]. Its products are consumables, over 90% of 2025 revenue came from products used in manufacturing or incorporated in devices, and about 70% of raw materials are sourced locally with no supplier above 10% of raw material spend, which reduces input and tariff risk [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. There is no sponsor and no documented creditor-adverse act since the separation [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Demand is concentrated and cancellable: the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, two named customers were about a tenth of sales each in 2026, and contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Adjusted Operating EBITDA excludes real cash costs, so operating cash flow less capex of USD 357 million trails company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million for nine months 2026 [CP-1; Documentary Fact from CP-1 figures]. Claims outside debt include a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities, tax indemnities and operating leases of USD 514 million, and the legacy exposure is not capped [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Shareholder returns of USD 125 million over nine months, with USD 425 million of repurchase authorization remaining, compete with debt reduction [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The term loan is floating-rate and no hedge is reported, so a 100 basis point move changes interest expense by USD 24 million a year [K p:82; Documentary Fact, added here]. Qnity has about eleven months of stand-alone results at September 30, 2026, so the trend in interest, tax and cost lines is not like-for-like with the carve-out periods [CP-0, CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Management's descriptions of itself as the premier provider and of consecutive profitable growth are Management Language and are not adopted [CP-1A].

### Readiness view

Nothing found blocks preparation or creates an unresolved identity boundary: every source names the same registrant, Qnity Electronics, Inc., and the first-page text of each source states a distinct period. The limits are: (a) the executed credit agreement, its first amendment and the two indentures are exhibits cited by reference and are not in the pack, so debt terms, guarantor mechanics and covenant definitions come only from filing summaries; (b) the annual report and the 2025 comparatives are presented on a carve-out basis for the period before the November 1, 2025 separation, and the release comparatives are pro forma; (c) no agency rating, market quote, valuation input or earnings presentation is supplied; (d) extraction is text only, so charts and images are not inspected. ## Next module

Run CP-1 next on the full pinned set, carrying forward these limits: label every figure by period (Q3 2026, nine months 2026, FY2025, and the pro forma or carve-out basis where it applies), take Q3 2026 facts from the filed 10-Q over the release, and record covenant terms as filer summaries only. CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 follow in the planned order. The next evidence action is to request the credit agreement, its first amendment and the indentures if covenant headroom or guarantor structure matters to the committee.

Module CP-1 (financial base) for Qnity Electronics, Inc. (issuer id q, NYSE: Q), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Perimeter: the consolidated registrant, Qnity Electronics, Inc. and its subsidiaries; the registrant is itself the issuer of the notes and the borrower under the credit agreement (no subsidiary-level issuer is named in the filings). Currency and unit: USD millions unless a cell says otherwise; ratios are in x. Periods follow the run context: current period Q3 2026 (quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026), prior period FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025). Nothing dated after the cutoff 2026-11-05 is used; the latest evidence is the release dated 2026-11-04. The task is to extract reported facts, separate them from calculations, build leverage, coverage, liquidity and maturity views, and state what the evidence cannot support. It is not a credit rating view.

Basis flags that apply to every number below: (1) Qnity was wholly owned by DuPont de Nemours, Inc. until the separation on November 1, 2025, so FY2025 and the nine months 2025 comparatives are carve-out statements with parent allocations and without most of the current debt; (2) from 2026 the issuer presents one caption, Transformation, integration and other charges, and recast the 2025 interim comparatives to it; (3) Adjusted Operating EBITDA is the company's own measure, defined in the filings as pre-tax earnings before interest, depreciation, amortization, non-operating pension items, foreign exchange, indirect legacy costs, and significant items.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage is moderate and fell: total debt is 2.37x LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA versus 2.79x at FY2025, with 2,362 of liquidity and a revolver undrawn to October 2030. Legacy and transformation cash costs sit outside that EBITDA. | Medium | Adjusted Operating EBITDA is a company measure; covenant EBITDA, the reported covenant ratio and 2026 cash interest are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage fell because LTM EBITDA rose while total debt was little changed. | Indicative first lien leverage at FY2025 was 1.69x against a 4.50:1.00 test, but the covenant definition is not supplied. | Medium |

| Nine-month operating cash flow less capex was 357 against company adjusted free cash flow of 607. | Legacy, transformation and tax-cost payments, not in adjusted figures, take real cash; 125 went to dividends and buybacks. | Medium |

| Interest expense is a new fixed cost: 186 for nine months 2026 against 14 in nine months 2025. | LTM cover on interest expense is 7.15x, and 6.62x on annualised latest-quarter interest; cash interest is not printed. | Medium |
| Indemnities to the former parent grew with a North Carolina settlement share. | These are cash claims outside debt; the filing says exposure could reach about 100 above the accrual. | Medium |

### Financial base view

The reported-fact base is adequate to underwrite a first view, and it is cleaner than the carve-out history suggests because the standalone capital structure has been in place since November 1, 2025. On filed figures, net sales were 4,300 for nine months 2026 against 3,564 a year earlier, and Adjusted Operating EBITDA was 1,345 against 1,091. Total debt of 4,019 at September 30, 2026 compares with 1,124 of cash and a fully undrawn 1,250 revolver (1,238 after letters of credit). Calculated leverage is 2.37x total and 1.71x net on LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA, down from 2.79x and 2.16x at FY2025. Three points temper this. First, the EBITDA measure excludes indirect legacy costs (84 in nine months 2026) and transformation, integration and other charges (123), which are real cash outflows. Second, interest cover on LTM interest expense flatters the run rate, because the LTM window includes a quarter in which the term loan was outstanding for only two months. Third, FY2025 and nine months 2025 are carve-out periods, so year-on-year changes in interest, tax and allocated costs mix a basis change with performance. The covenant headroom cannot be read from the sources: the maintenance test and its level are disclosed, the issuer's reported ratio and its covenant EBITDA definition are not.

### Definition review

Adjusted Operating EBITDA is defined as pre-tax earnings before interest, depreciation, amortization, non-operating pension and OPEB items, foreign exchange gains and losses, indirect legacy costs and significant items (Q3 p:39). It is not covenant EBITDA, and it is not a GAAP measure. It adds back items that were cash costs in nine months 2026: indirect legacy costs (84 in the income statement; 114 of cash in the release free-cash-flow bridge, R3 p:11), transformation, integration and other charges (123 in the income statement; 84 of cash, R3 p:11) and a foreign tax cost of the separation (52, R3 p:11). The release prints Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 607 for nine months 2026 against calculated operating cash flow less capex of 357; the difference is these three items (see Calculations). The company's total debt (4,019) is carrying value, net of unamortized discount and issuance costs; the face value of notes and term loan is about 4,100 at December 31, 2025 (K p:120). Net sales and EBITDA comparatives in the releases for Q3 2025 are pro forma (R3 p:2) and are not used.
### Conflicts and consistency

No numeric conflict was found between the 10-Q Q3 2026 statements and the Q3 2026 release (net sales, net income, cash, debt, operating cash flow and capex agree). The release shows two Q3 2025 EBITDA figures (382 unadjusted in the reconciliation, 370 pro forma in the headline); this module uses the unadjusted one because it is on the same carve-out basis as the filed 10-Q comparatives. The 2026 expense caption (Transformation, integration and other charges) differs from the two FY2025 10-K captions; this is a presentation change, and no number is contradicted.

Module CP-1A (business and transaction context) for Qnity Electronics, Inc. (issuer id q, NYSE: Q), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, public case. The reader question is which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor. The drivers are: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. The chain used for every material conclusion is evidence (a located quote), then risk mechanic, then credit implication. Currency is USD; periods follow the run context (current Q3 2026, prior FY2025). Nothing after the cutoff 2026-11-05 is used. This module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion. Fact rows carry one of four tags: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, or Insufficient Information. Figures are taken from the quoted source or from the accepted financial base handoff, and are not recomputed here.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Qnity is a newly independent, widely held supplier of consumable semiconductor and interconnect materials with no sponsor. Debt was raised at separation and paid to the former parent, to which Qnity also owes indemnity payments. | Medium | No presentations, transcripts or executed separation and debt documents are supplied, so transaction terms rest on filing narrative. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt was raised at separation and paid to the former parent as a cash dividend. | The leverage was set by the separation, not by operations; creditors rely on later cash generation to reduce it. | High |

| There is no sponsor or controlling holder; one preferred share, issued to DuPont and placed in a trust, has protective rights. | No sponsor extraction risk is documented, but consent rights over charter and capital changes sit with that trust. | Medium |

| The top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales and contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments. | Revenue is volume-driven and cancellable; a single large customer loss could move results. | High |
| Qnity pays 44% of certain DuPont legacy liabilities, including PFAS settlements. | These payments are cash claims outside debt that can rise with settlements. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Qnity Electronics, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated supplier of consumable materials to semiconductor fabrication and to electronics interconnect, reported in two segments, Semiconductor Technologies and Interconnect Solutions. It became independent on November 1, 2025 through a pro-rata distribution by DuPont de Nemours, Inc., and its shares have traded on the New York Stock Exchange since November 3, 2025. The credit-relevant structure is a stand-alone, widely held company with no sponsor, whose debt was raised just before the distribution, at the issuer level with subsidiary guarantees, and was paid out to the former parent. The debt amount was set in connection with the separation. Operating strength is evident in the filings: volume-led sales growth in both segments, driven by AI-linked demand in advanced nodes, advanced packaging and thermal management, and a consumable revenue model. Two features constrain the creditor view. First, customer contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments and the top ten customers are concentrated, so revenue visibility rests on customer forecasts that can be cancelled. Second, Qnity has contractually taken on a share of DuPont's legacy liabilities and some tax exposure under agreements negotiated before it had an independent board. Post-separation behaviour is documented as a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase programme, a borrower-favourable term loan repricing and debt amortization. No document shows priming, uptiering, drop-downs or collateral release. Missing is any executed document or management presentation, so terms and management's own capital allocation priorities are visible only through filing summaries.

| Revenue streams and model | Substantially all revenue is product sales to manufacturers and distributors; over 90% of 2025 revenue came from products used in manufacturing or incorporated in final devices. | Documentary Fact | Q3 p:11; K p:7. Consumable revenue follows customer fab utilisation, not capital cycles. |

| Revenue visibility | Contracts with top customers do not contain long-term purchase commitments; customers may cancel orders or change quantities. | Documentary Fact | K p:17. Forecast-based, cancellable demand limits revenue visibility. |

| Pricing and volume drivers | Net sales growth in Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 was primarily due to volume; local price and product mix was nil in total in both periods. | Documentary Fact | Q3 p:35. Growth is volume-led, so it depends on end-market demand and share, not price. |

| End-market demand narrative | Management attributes volume to AI-driven technology ramps, advanced packaging, AI PCBs and thermal management. | Management Language | Q3 p:40. Promotional causality; treat as management's attribution, not a measured driver. |

| Cost structure | Cost of sales was 53% of net sales for nine months 2026 against 54% a year earlier; R&D and SG&A were 7% and 13% in both years. | Documentary Fact | Q3 p:35, p:36. Cost ratios stable, so margin gain came mainly from cost of sales leverage. |

Amounts are in the financial base (CP-1). Growth capex competes with debt reduction. |
| Working capital | Higher trade receivables and inventory in 2026 on increased sales, net of higher payables. | Documentary Fact | Q3 p:42. Growth consumes working capital. |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The defining transaction is the separation of Qnity from DuPont de Nemours, Inc., announced on May 22, 2024 and completed on November 1, 2025 by a pro-rata distribution of one Qnity share for every two DuPont shares held on the record date of October 22, 2025 (K p:6). Qnity common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on November 3, 2025. There is no sponsor and no change-of-control transaction in the sources, and no acquisition or disposal of a business is reported in the 2026 filings read for this module. The annual report states that Qnity may pursue bolt-on and strategic acquisitions (K p:17), which is intent, not an event.

New debt was raised in two steps before the distribution. On August 15, 2025 the issuer sold senior secured notes due 2032 and senior unsecured notes due 2033, each guaranteed by every subsidiary that is a borrower or guarantor under the credit facilities, with the secured notes sharing first-priority liens pari passu with the credit facilities (K p:116 to p:118). On October 31, 2025 it entered a credit agreement for a seven-year term loan and a five-year revolving facility, and the annual report states that the full term loan, together with the notes proceeds, was paid directly to DuPont as a cash dividend in connection with the separation (K p:119). The aggregate principal incurred in connection with the spin-off is stated as 4.1 billion (K p:43), and the financial base handoff carries the instrument-level terms, the maturities and the liquidity position. The use of proceeds is therefore a documented distribution to the former parent, recorded in the cash flow statement as net transfers to the parent. This is a debt-funded distribution at separation, made when the parent still controlled the subsidiary and set its terms; the annual report states Qnity had no independent board or management team representing its interests while the separation agreements were negotiated (K p:45).

Since the distribution the documented actions are a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase authorization, a repricing of the term loan and scheduled amortization. The repricing, effective July 1, 2026, cut the margin on term SOFR borrowings from 2.00% to 1.75% with no material change to principal, maturity, amortization or covenant structure, and carries a 1.00% premium on repricing events for six months (Q3 p:20); it is a borrower-favourable amendment to a creditor-owned instrument, not a creditor-adverse one. The amendment document itself is not supplied. Liquidity effect: the financial base shows an undrawn revolver and cash, with no facility expiring within twelve months. Status of every transaction item is final and closed; the only open items are contingent legacy payments to DuPont described under governance below.

Behaviour is assessed at issuer level, from documented actions only. Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility are kept separate.

Fundamental credit synthesis for Qnity Electronics, Inc. (issuer id q), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, built on the accepted source-readiness, financial-base and business-and-transaction handoffs. Scope is business risk, financial risk and liquidity, and the gaps that limit them; relative value, instrument selection and recovery outcomes are out of scope.

| CP-1A | d3761351f4065b283710e460f89b4ed8f93cac8e525e2385ab9e69bd8c32ae8c | Business, ownership, transaction and governance facts. Its readiness judgment of this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, which keeps confidence below High. |

One extension to the financial base: it does not carry the issuer's floating-rate sensitivity. The annual report states that a 100 basis point move in the weighted average rate would change annual interest expense by USD 24 million on the term loan (K p:82), and that interest rate risk arises primarily from that variable-rate loan (K p:81). This is used below and is labelled as added here. No figure in the earlier handoffs is contradicted.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Qnity has a moderate-leverage, well-funded credit profile: total debt is 2.37x LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA and liquidity is 2,362. Cancellable, concentrated demand and cash costs outside adjusted EBITDA are the main weaknesses. | Medium | Covenant terms, the reported covenant ratio, 2026 cash interest and the executed debt documents are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x, down from 2.79x at FY2025, with no large maturity before 2032. | Refinancing pressure is low, and a 32.3% fall in EBITDA would be needed to reach 3.5x. | Medium |
| Nine-month operating cash flow less capex was 357, against company adjusted free cash flow of 607. | Cash available for debt reduction is lower than adjusted figures imply. | Medium |
| The top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales and contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments. | Earnings can fall quickly in a demand downturn, and leverage is sensitive to that. | High |

| Qnity pays 44% of certain DuPont legacy liabilities, and the term loan is variable-rate. | Legacy payments, and a 100 basis point rate move worth 24 a year, add cash claims outside the adjusted measure. | Medium |
### Credit view

Qnity Electronics, Inc. has a moderate-leverage, well-funded credit profile with earnings quality that is weaker than the headline ratios suggest. The strongest support is financial: total debt of USD 4,019 million is 2.37x LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA, liquidity is USD 2,362 million, the revolver is undrawn to October 2030 and no large maturity falls before 2032. The weakest point is the durability of the cash behind those ratios. Demand is volume-driven, cancellable and concentrated in a few customers, adjusted EBITDA leaves out legacy and transformation cash costs, and a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities sits outside debt. The outcome will be decided by whether AI-linked volume growth persists while cash after interest, legacy payments and shareholder returns keeps reducing leverage. Covenant headroom cannot be verified from the sources.
### Key findings

First, leverage fell and liquidity is ample. Qnity Electronics, Inc. reports total debt of USD 4,019 million against cash of USD 1,124 million and a fully undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver (USD 1,238 million after letters of credit), so liquidity is USD 2,362 million [CP-1]. Total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x, down from 2.79x at FY2025, and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x against 2.16x. Debt maturities are USD 24 million a year to 2030 and USD 3,980 million after that, so the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033, beyond the revolver's October 2030 expiry. The mechanism is that EBITDA grew while debt was little changed; the implication is low near-term refinancing risk and a cushion against an earnings shortfall.

Second, the adjusted measures overstate cash available for creditors. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow less capex was USD 357 million, against company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million; the USD 250 million difference is transformation cash costs, indirect legacy payments to DuPont and a separation foreign tax cost [CP-1]. Qnity also paid USD 125 million in dividends and buybacks in the same period. Debt reduction therefore depends on cash that is smaller than adjusted figures show and is shared with shareholders, with the restricted payment baskets not known.

Third, revenue visibility is short. Customer contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments, the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, and most sales are in Asia Pacific [CP-1A]. Growth in 2026 has been primarily volume, attributed by management to AI-driven demand. A cut in orders by one large customer would reach earnings quickly through lost absorption, and leverage is sensitive to that: LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA would have to fall 21.0% for total debt to reach 3.0x and 32.3% to reach 3.5x (illustrative thresholds, not covenants).

Fourth, claims outside debt are material and growing. Qnity bears 44% of certain DuPont legacy liabilities, including PFAS settlements; the 10-Q states exposure could be up to about USD 100 million above the amount accrued, and a new North Carolina settlement added to the accrual in 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The Tax Matters Agreement can add tax indemnities if the spin-off fails to qualify as tax-free. These are senior-ranking cash claims that sit outside the debt figure.

Fifth, interest is a new and partly floating cost. Interest expense was USD 237 million over the last twelve months and USD 64 million in Q3 2026, so LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA covers annualised latest-quarter interest 6.62x and LTM interest expense 7.15x [CP-1]. The term loan carries a variable rate, and the annual report states that a 100 basis point change would move annual interest expense by USD 24 million (K p:82); no hedge is reported in the pinned filings. Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026, so a cash-basis cover ratio cannot be built.

Sixth, the capital structure came from the separation. The term loan and note proceeds were paid to DuPont as a cash dividend, and Qnity had no independent board while the separation agreements were negotiated [CP-1A]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented since; the July 2026 repricing lowered the borrowing margin without changing security or maturity. Capacity to make distributions or incur debt cannot be tested because the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Qnity Electronics, Inc. has moderate and falling leverage: total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x [CP-1; Documentary Fact from a CP-1 figure]. It has deep liquidity of USD 2,362 million, with no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 785 million of its USD 1,124 million cash held in foreign subsidiaries, which may limit how much is freely available in the United States [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its debt is long-dated, with scheduled amortisation of about USD 24 million a year and the notes and term loan due in 2032 and 2033 [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its operating base is growing on volume in both segments, with an LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA margin of 30.9% on USD 5,490 million of LTM net sales [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact, with the margin a company measure]. Its products are consumables, over 90% of 2025 revenue came from products used in manufacturing or incorporated in devices, and about 70% of raw materials are sourced locally with no supplier above 10% of raw material spend, which reduces input and tariff risk [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. There is no sponsor and no documented creditor-adverse act since the separation [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation].

Weaknesses. Demand is concentrated and cancellable: the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, two named customers were about a tenth of sales each in 2026, and contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Adjusted Operating EBITDA excludes real cash costs, so operating cash flow less capex of USD 357 million trails company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million for nine months 2026 [CP-1; Documentary Fact from CP-1 figures]. Claims outside debt include a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities, tax indemnities and operating leases of USD 514 million, and the legacy exposure is not capped [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Shareholder returns of USD 125 million over nine months, with USD 425 million of repurchase authorization remaining, compete with debt reduction [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The term loan is floating-rate and no hedge is reported, so a 100 basis point move changes interest expense by USD 24 million a year [K p:82; Documentary Fact, added here]. Qnity has about eleven months of stand-alone results at September 30, 2026, so the trend in interest, tax and cost lines is not like-for-like with the carve-out periods [CP-0, CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Management's descriptions of itself as the premier provider and of consecutive profitable growth are Management Language and are not adopted [CP-1A].
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Moderate leverage and strong liquidity, offset by short revenue visibility, cash costs outside adjusted EBITDA and legacy claims outside debt | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and maturity tables; CP-1A credit translations and fact register |

| Thesis | A well-funded, moderately levered materials supplier whose creditors depend on continued AI-linked volume growth and on cash, not adjusted earnings, to reduce leverage after a debt-funded separation | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above |

| Confidence limit | Below High because the business-and-transaction handoff judged this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and covenant, document and ratings evidence is missing | Insufficient Information on the limits | Not applicable | CP-0 gaps; CP-1A consumer judgment |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Demand downturn or loss of a large customer | Concentrated, cancellable, volume-driven revenue with high operating leverage in a cyclical end market | Earnings and cash would fall faster than debt; leverage would rise (a fall of 32.3% in EBITDA reaches 3.5x) | Material |

| Cash leakage outside adjusted EBITDA | Legacy payments to DuPont, transformation cost and separation tax sit outside the company's adjusted measures | Cash for debt reduction is smaller than adjusted figures imply; free cash flow is the better monitor | Material |

| Legacy liability growth | Settlements by DuPont, Chemours and Corteva flow to Qnity at a fixed 44% share, with exposure above the accrual stated | Senior-ranking cash claims outside debt could rise and reduce liquidity headroom | Material |

| Shareholder distributions and capacity | Dividends and a USD 500 million repurchase authorization with a large remaining balance, under baskets that are not supplied | Cash to creditors could be diverted, and capacity cannot be tested | Material |
| Variable-rate interest | The term loan floats over SOFR; a 100 basis point move is USD 24 million a year (added here) | Higher rates cut cover; no hedge is reported | Minor |
| Refinancing | Notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033 | Low within the near term; the revolver expires in October 2030 and is undrawn | Minor |
| Documentation and covenant visibility | Maintenance test and baskets known only through summaries | Headroom and distribution limits cannot be verified | Material |
## Calculations

All inputs are the figures in the financial base handoff (USD millions unless stated) and were checked to the filings when that handoff was accepted. The first group recomputes figures carried above; the second group is new.
| Id | Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| R1 | Total debt / LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA | 4,019 / 1,695 | 2.37x |
| R2 | Net debt / LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA | (4,019 - 1,124) / 1,695 = 2,895 / 1,695 | 1.71x |

| R7 | Shareholder returns, nine months 2026 | 50 + 75 | 125 |

| R9 | LTM EBITDA / annualised latest-quarter interest | 1,695 / (64 x 4) | 6.62x |
| N1 | EBITDA fall to reach 3.0x total debt / EBITDA (illustrative, not a covenant) | 4,019 / 3.0 = 1,339.7; 1 - 1,339.7 / 1,695 | 21.0% |
| N4 | LTM EBITDA less LTM capex, over LTM interest expense | (1,695 - 361) / 237 = 1,334 / 237 | 5.63x |

| N6 | Net debt over LTM operating cash flow less capex (years, before shareholder returns) | 2,895 / 777 | 3.73 |
| N7 | Floating-rate sensitivity, 100 basis points on the term loan (K p:82) | Stated as USD 24 million; check 1.00% x 2,350 = 23.5 | 24 |

Direction checks: leverage fell because LTM EBITDA of 1,695 exceeds FY2025 EBITDA of 1,441 while total debt moved from 4,027 to 4,019. Nine-month operating cash flow of 647 is below 782 a year earlier. Illustrative thresholds N1 to N3 are not covenant levels.
## Gaps

| Executed credit agreement, First Amendment and indentures are not supplied; covenant EBITDA and the issuer's reported first lien net leverage ratio are Not supplied. | Headroom to the maintenance test, distribution baskets and guarantor mechanics cannot be verified; this limits the confidence in the whole credit view. | Material | Obtain the exhibits and a compliance certificate. |

## Next module

CP-5 should trace every figure in this synthesis to the financial base handoff and the floating-rate extension to K p:81 and p:82, check that the three illustrative leverage thresholds are labelled as non-covenant, and keep Management Language and Insufficient Information tags intact.
